posts.author: Johnfp
posts.content_md: I was thinking this morning, has anyone tried to sandwich 3 or 4 holographic films together inside of the two glass plates and make a single exposure thus creating 4 holograms on 4 separate films at the same time? I know each hologram would be displaced by the thickness of the film relative to one another and you would get a slight difference in ref:obj light ratios from the first to the last film. But I do believe it would work and it shure would save time in creating a "lot" of a image hologram.

posts.author: Tony
posts.content_md: Are you talking 3-4 masters sandwiched together John?

posts.author: Johnfp
posts.content_md:
NO, but that surely would be another thought. 

I was thinking making 3 or 4 copies from a master in an H1 to H2 imaged plane set up. 3 or 4 pieces of unexposed film would be sandwiched together and exposed simutaneously from the master and a ref beam.

posts.author: Ed Wesly
posts.content_md:
I know if works for two, as I have done it accidentally. The major objection I can see to this concept is the amount of scatter that could be picked up by light going through all those emulsions.

If you can afford to make a stack of 3 or 4 films, just cut some pieces small enough for one of your eyes to look through, and look at the reference beam. (I am assuming everyone here can figure out how to do this safely!) If the pinhole does not look sharp, like a halo around it, the fringes might lose some contrast and make a poor recording!

posts.author: Johnfp
posts.content_md:
Well, it wont be long before the weather warms and I can get back into my third world basement to make holograms. 

Thanks Ed, I am going to give it a try. I think I will try two first then three and work myself up. What the heck right, I got to do something off the wall. 

I also do not index match, so someone that index matches may be able to do more then what I find I can do.

Tony, back to your thought. That would be a good way of combining images and/or having images occupy the same space. I leave it up to everyone to decide how to use that in their artistic expressions.

posts.author: BobH
posts.content_md: I've made transfers from three 12x16" transmission masters simultaneously in the past, and it worked OK. I used glass plates and no index matching at the time, but would certainly index match now. No reason to not, and huge improvement in noise would result. At least use baby oil.
